title: Palindrome Partitioning IV
summary: Determine if a string can be divided into three non-empty palindromic substrings.
statement: Determine if a string can be divided into three non-empty palindromic substrings. Return true if possible, otherwise return false. A string is a palindrome if it reads the same backward as forward.
constraints: Split s into exactly three nonempty contiguous substrings.
Return whether all three substrings can be palindromes.
hints: Only palindrome status for substrings and two cut positions matter.
Precompute palindrome intervals, then enumerate the two cuts.
Fill pal[left][right] from matching endpoints and the inner interval; test pal[0][i], pal[i+1][j], and pal[j+1][n-1].
Every three-part split has exactly one cut pair, so the enumeration accepts exactly when one pair has three palindrome intervals.
editorial: Every three-part split has exactly one cut pair, so the enumeration accepts exactly when one pair has three palindrome intervals.

tests.explanation: The split a | bcb | dd consists entirely of palindromes.
No two cut positions produce three palindromic pieces.
